rows.name: TRON_LOG_LEVEL
rows.values: One of `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `warning`, `err`, `error`, `critical`, `off`, in lower case. Any other text, for example `INFO`, counts as `off`.
rows.default: Unset: `debug`. Empty: counts as `off`. The program then writes no log messages.
rows.effect: Sets the lowest message level that the program writes. The level applies to the log file and to the output on stderr. With `off`, the program writes no log messages, error messages included.
rows.notes: No log line prints the level in effect. `SPDLOG_LEVEL` is applied after it. `SPDLOG_LEVEL` can hide more messages. It cannot show messages below this level. `rinzler` keeps its HTTP library at level warn. Five test programs read the name themselves, with `info` as default.

rows.name: TRON_LOG_PLACEMENT
rows.values: Any value turns it on. The text is not parsed. The values `0` and `false` also turn it on.
rows.default: Unset: off. No placement count is kept. Empty: on.
rows.effect: While a model loads, the program counts the tiles (blocks of a weight tensor) that it places, per tensor name and per FPGA card. At the end of the placement it writes one info log entry that starts with `Tensor device counts:`. The counts follow as JSON.
rows.notes: A `TRON_LOG_LEVEL` of `warn` or higher hides the entry. The entry spans several lines. The JSON names each card by its index in the process. When the variable is set, the code also aborts if a tile is placed before a tensor name is given.

evidence.quote: // To log placement, define the TRON_LOG_PLACEMENT environment variable.

rows.name: TRON_MAX_LOGITS_CHUNK_SIZE
rows.values: Integer of 1 or more, parsed with `atol`. The unit is listeners (callbacks that wait for the result of one token). Text that is not a number counts as `0`.
rows.default: Unset: the chunk size equals the number of workers of the shared thread pool. Empty: counts as `0`.
rows.effect: Limits the logits chunk size. The chunk size is the smaller of this value and the number of workers of the shared thread pool (the worker threads for model work on the CPU). Each forward pass computes logits for one chunk of listeners at a time.
rows.notes: The code does not reject `0`. With a chunk size of 0 listeners, the first forward pass divides by zero. A negative number sets no limit. The process reads the value once. No log line prints the chunk size.

rows.name: TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS
rows.values: Integer of 0 or more, parsed with `atol`. The unit is worker threads. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. A negative number becomes a very large number.
rows.default: Unset: half of the workers of the shared thread pool, rounded down. Empty: counts as `0`.
rows.effect: Sets the largest number of main helpers in a forward pass, and `0` turns main helpers off. A main helper is a worker of the shared thread pool (the worker threads for model work on the CPU) that helps the main thread with non-attention work. The other workers run attention.
rows.notes: A value below `TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS` or its default aborts the process at model load with `Expected min_main_helpers <= max_main_helpers`. With 16 or more pool workers, `0` also needs `TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS=0`. The pool size is not checked. A forward pass that leaves no attention worker aborts the process.

evidence.quote: if (const char* env = getenv("TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS")) return atol(env);
return app_pool().num_workers() / 2;  // Reserve half the workers for attention

rows.name: TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS
rows.values: Integer of 0 or more, parsed with `atol`. The unit is worker threads. Text that is not a number counts as `0`. A negative number becomes a very large number.
rows.default: Unset: 1 helper when the shared thread pool has 16 or more workers. Otherwise 0 helpers. Empty: counts as `0`.
rows.effect: Sets the smallest number of main helpers in a forward pass. A main helper is a worker of the shared thread pool (the worker threads for model work on the CPU) that helps the main thread with non-attention work. The other workers run attention.
rows.notes: A value above `TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS` or its default aborts the process at model load with `Expected min_main_helpers <= max_main_helpers`. A pass with few tokens can use fewer helpers. The pool size is not checked. A pass that leaves no attention worker aborts the process.

evidence.quote: if (const char* env = getenv("TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS")) return atol(env);
if (app_pool().num_workers() >= 16)  // typically true in TP4 but not TP2
return 1;                          // Force at least one main helper by default.

rows.name: TRON_NO_PREQUANT_CACHE
rows.read_by: `t_prequant_cache`, a test program (`h/tron/hardware/prequant_cache.hpp`). No product program reads it.
rows.values: Any non-empty text other than `0` turns the switch on. `no` and `false` also turn it on. An empty value and `0` leave it off.
rows.effect: The function `prequant_cache_disabled()` returns `true`. No product program calls this function, and `rinzler` and `runtron` behave the same with and without the variable. The prequant cache is an on-disk store of quantized model weights for later loads.
rows.notes: Only `t/t_prequant_cache.cpp` includes the header that holds the function.

rows.name: TRON_NO_RTM
rows.values: Exactly `1` turns Intel RTM off. Every other text leaves RTM on.
rows.default: Unset: the wait code uses Intel RTM when the CPU is an Intel CPU that reports RTM.
rows.effect: On an Intel CPU with RTM (the TSX transactional memory instructions), the wait code stops using RTM. Each wait step is then a `pause` instruction. The startup log states that decode is 13 to 30 percent slower and that the setting is for benchmarking only, never for production.
rows.notes: It has no effect on AMD CPUs or on Intel CPUs without RTM. When it takes effect, startup logs the error text `Intel RTM (TSX) DISABLED by TRON_NO_RTM=1`. With RTM in use, startup logs `INIT: Intel RTM (TSX) supported`. The test `t_mwaitx_cliff` reads it too.

evidence.quote: spdlog::error("INIT: *** Intel RTM (TSX) DISABLED by TRON_NO_RTM=1   ***");

rows.name: TRON_PERF_INTERVAL_SEC
rows.values: Number of seconds, parsed with `std::stof`. `0` means off. A negative number writes the line after every forward pass. Text that does not start with a number makes `std::stof` throw.
rows.default: Unset: `0` seconds. No line is written. Empty: `std::stof` throws, and the process terminates at its first forward pass.
rows.effect: After a forward pass, the program writes one info log line when at least this many seconds have passed after the previous line. The line gives the passes, tokens, logits, elapsed seconds and tokens per second of that interval.
rows.notes: The line starts with `Completed <n> passes with <n> tokens`. It does not name the model. An invalid value terminates the process at the end of its first forward pass, not at startup. A `TRON_LOG_LEVEL` of `warn` or higher hides the line.

evidence.quote: spdlog::info("Completed {} passes with {} tokens for {} logits in {} s.  "

rows.name: TRON_PER_USER_PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT
rows.values: Integer of 1 or more, parsed with `std::stoul`. The unit is tokens. Text that does not start with a number makes `std::stoul` throw.
rows.default: Unset: 128 tokens. Empty: `std::stoul` throws, and the process terminates when it handles its first prompt.
rows.effect: Sets the largest number of prompt tokens that one request submits for processing in one step. A longer prompt is processed in several chunks of this size.
rows.notes: An invalid value terminates the process when it handles its first prompt, not at startup. The code does not reject `0`. With `0` the prompt position does not advance. `bin/analyze-tps` sets `10000` or `128` tokens. No log line prints the value.

rows.name: TRON_SPEEDOMETER_PRIOR_STRENGTH
rows.values: Number without a unit, parsed with `std::atof`. It must be 0 or above. Text that is not a number counts as `0`.
rows.effect: Sets how strongly each update moves the speed estimate of each worker of the shared thread pool (the worker threads for model work on the CPU) toward the mean of all workers. `0` removes this effect. The estimates split the attention work between the workers that run attention.
rows.notes: At each update the mean of all workers gets the weight `1-exp(-value/timescale)`. The timescale is `TRON_SPEEDOMETER_TIMESCALE` or its default of 10 updates. A negative value aborts the process with `Expected prior_strength >= 0.0f`. The estimates are not used when the model config sets `pay_for_determinism`.

evidence.quote: size_t num_workers, float timescale = 10.0f, float prior_strength = 0.1f)

rows.name: TRON_SPEEDOMETER_TIMESCALE
rows.values: Number, parsed with `std::atof`. The unit is updates of the speed estimator. It must be above 0. Text that is not a number counts as `0`.
rows.default: Unset: `10` updates. Empty: counts as `0`, and the process aborts.
rows.effect: Sets the time constant of the speed estimator of the shared thread pool (the worker threads for model work on the CPU). At each update, the estimator multiplies its stored measurements by `exp(-(1+p)/value)`, where `p` is `TRON_SPEEDOMETER_PRIOR_STRENGTH`. A larger value makes the speed estimates change more slowly.
rows.notes: The speed estimates split the attention work between workers. A value of 0 or below aborts the process with `Expected timescale > 0.0f`. `TRON_SPEEDOMETER_PRIOR_STRENGTH` is divided by this value. There is one update per forward pass. A model config with `pay_for_determinism` ignores the estimates.

evidence.quote: size_t num_workers, float timescale = 10.0f, float prior_strength = 0.1f)

rows.name: TRON_TOKENIZE_PY
rows.values: Path of an executable tokenizer program. The text is used as given. If the path does not exist, the program aborts with `Python tokenizer script <path> not found`.
rows.default: Unset: the programs run `bin/tokenize_py`, relative to their working directory. In a Nix dev shell, `make gen/tokenize_py` stops with an error.
rows.effect: Names the program that the Python fallback tokenizer runs as a child process to read the vocabulary and to encode text. In a Nix dev shell, `make gen/tokenize_py` copies this file to `gen/tokenize_py`.
rows.notes: The fallback is used when the model directory has no `tokenizer.json`, when the Rust tokenizer fails to load, or when `USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER` or `VALIDATE_TOKENIZERS` is enabled. The warning `Falling back to slow tokenizer script <path>` shows the path in effect. The Nix dev shell sets it.

evidence.quote: "Python tokenizer script {} not found; run in the tron source directory or "

new_terms.definition: One run of the model over a batch of tokens.
The scores that the model gives to each possible next token.
A callback that waits for the result of one token at the end of a forward pass. Most listeners receive the logits for the next token.

The worker threads that one rinzler or runtron process uses for model work on the CPU. It has one worker fewer than the number of application CPU cores of the process. The info log line `App CPU list:` shows these cores.
A worker of the shared thread pool that helps the main thread with non-attention work during a forward pass.
A worker of the shared thread pool that runs attention work during a forward pass. Every worker that is not a main helper is an attention worker.
The code (`speedometer_t`) that estimates the speed of each worker of the shared thread pool from measured work and time.
One block of a weight tensor. The program places each tile on FPGA cards as a unit.
An on-disk store of quantized model weights. A later load of the same model can read them back.
The transactional memory instructions of Intel CPUs. The code names them RTM (TSX). The TRON wait code uses them to make a thread wait for a change in memory.
The slow tokenizer that runs a Python program as a child process. TRON uses it when the Rust tokenizer is not available or when a variable asks for it.

notes: All 12 rows are kept and none is dropped. Every evidence quote was compared with its line in the checkout and all match. TRON_LOG_LEVEL: the level names, the rule that unknown text counts as off, and the rule that SPDLOG_LEVEL changes only the logger level come from spdlog v1.17.0. The checkout pins that version (cmake/versions.cmake:5) and downloads it at build time (CMakeLists.txt:275-280). It does not hold the spdlog source. The three rules were read again in a local copy of spdlog v1.17.0 outside the checkout and they hold (common-inl.h from_str, registry-inl.h set_levels). TRON_NO_PREQUANT_CACHE: no product program reads it at this commit. The only caller of the reader is the test t_prequant_cache. The row stays with for=developers. It can move to a test section. TRON_MAX_LOGITS_CHUNK_SIZE and TRON_PER_USER_PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT: the statements about the value 0 come from reading the code. Nothing was run. TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS and TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS: the abort for a helper count that leaves no attention worker also comes from reading the code. Audience: TRON_MAX_LOGITS_CHUNK_SIZE stays with operators as in the derivation record, although no comment, document or script names it. The two speed estimator variables stay with developers. TRON_PERF_INTERVAL_SEC: the line that proves that 0 means off is h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:232. It is not quoted as evidence. Its text holds the pipe character. rinzler_host and rinzler_mock are left out of read_by. The glossary does not define them. Pool size: the helper rows and the chunk size row depend on the number of pool workers. The info log line App CPU list (src/system/system.cpp:476) shows the application CPU cores, and the pool has one worker fewer (h/tron/threading.hpp:754-755). This is recorded in the new term shared thread pool.

At each update, the estimator multiplies its stored measurements by `exp(-(1+p)/value)`, where `p` is `TRON_SPEEDOMETER_PRIOR_STRENGTH`. A larger value makes the speed estimates change more slowly.
